setlist_extra.title: Take a Step Back / Funiculi Funicula

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Music Never Stopped** (2 reviews): Features a trippy midsection and a huge closing Garcia solo; the first-set highlight; Around 5:05 of the mid-song jam, Garcia lands on a repeating phrase while the band boils beneath him [13][15]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (2 reviews): Around ten minutes in they move into Fire with subdued wah and a seven-note Garcia figure, Weir's slide underneath; Garcia plays wildly in both solos, with emotional vocals on the chorus [9][13]
- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): A Jed that keeps building higher and higher [13]
- **Passenger** (1 review): First set could have ended at Passenger, but Brown Eyed Women and Music Never Stopped closed it instead [11]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Garcia's solo picks out many interesting notes; around five minutes the band settles in and Donna scats for nearly four minutes [9]

## The recordings

- **gd78-05-07.glassberg.vernon.18672.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 23 songs; 189 min; rated 3.8/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd78-05-07.sony.vernon.8763.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 199 min; rated 4.4/5 by 5 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording with crowd audible, crisp music, but low bass [19]
- **gd1978-05-07.fob.glassberg.motb.83498.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 21 songs; 197 min; rated 4.33/5 by 6 [4]
- **gd1978-05-07.152545.aud.petrunis.flac1644**: audience recording; 21 songs; 195 min [5]. Said about its sound: Tape is worn in spots but gives a different perspective, as if from the stands [5]
- **gd78-05-07.sbd.vernon.8327.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 172 min; rated 4.59/5 by 22 [6]. Said about its sound: Audience is faintly audible in the background at the start of Scarlet, and a brief garbled patch occurs in the first half minute; Recording is excellent until the end of Black Peter, when it abruptly turns loud and mostly audience, like being there; Dropouts are infrequent and tolerable; performance and sound are rated top notch [9][10][11][12][14]
- **gd1978-05-07.sbd.vernon.tetzeli.patch-8327.80126.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 172 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [7]

## Around the show

- The RPI Fieldhouse is a hockey rink with poor acoustics [10]
- Second set features stage banter worth listening for, including some before Estimated Prophet at the end of Fire [11]
- RPI Field House also hosted Frank Zappa in 1976, Boston in 1977, and Emerson Lake & Palmer in February 1978 [23]
- Reviewer calls the first set one of the best they have heard; the second is well played [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd78-05-07.glassberg.vernon.18672.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by John Steinthal; source: Audience Recording: NAK CM700, Sony 158SD [1]
- **gd78-05-07.sony.vernon.8763.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Unkown; source: Audience Recording [3]
- **gd1978-05-07.fob.glassberg.motb.83498.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by A. Egert and D. McCabe; source: Audience FOB Recording. Nakamichi CM300's > Sony 158SD > MAC [4]. Also: First 1:13 of Jack Straw was patched from the Sony Vernon 8763 source, using a five-second crossfade [4]
- **gd1978-05-07.152545.aud.petrunis.flac1644**: taped by Concert recording by Rich Petrunis.; transferred by Transferred by Andrew F. 05/2021; source: Stereo mic & recorder (models unknown) > TDK AD-90's (normal bias) cassettes. [5]. Also: Patches from ID-8763 cover Jack Straw, It's All Over Now, Scarlet, Drums, and Around and Around through the end; tapes shared by John and Rich Petrunis [5]
- **gd78-05-07.sbd.vernon.8327.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard with Audience patches [6]
- **gd1978-05-07.sbd.vernon.tetzeli.patch-8327.80126.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Bill Tetzeli; source: SBDMC>PCM>DAT>CD w/Aud MC>DAT>CD [7]. Also: About 35 seconds between He's Gone and Drums were patched from the 8763 download; Matt Vernon taped, Dale Shepherd circulated [7]
